title: The tumor suppressor menin is a key scaffold mediator for homologous recombination repair.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed all four processed tables from the two GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series: GSE302950_Men1vsWT.xls.gz (772 genes, 25 columns, only rows labelled Up/Down), GSE302950_MLLvsWT.xls.gz (3,956 genes, every adjusted p-value < 0.05, no per-sample columns), GSE230855_M_KOvsM_WT_deg_all.txt.gz (130 genes), GSE230855_gene_fpkm.txt.gz (54,532 genes x 8 macrophage samples). Also read both GEO series records: 14 samples in GSE302950 and 8 in GSE230855, all mouse.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The biology (menin binding gamma-H2A.X through its Val371-Gln400 motif, SETD2 recruitment, H3K36me3 rewriting, DNA end resection) rests entirely on gel, microscopy and reporter-assay figures with no deposited numeric tables. The whole-exome sequencing deposit (ScienceDB DOI 10.57760/sciencedb.28014) resolves to a live page but its file listing would not render or return through the API, so sample count and file types there are unverified.

a1_downloadable.note: Both GEO series are public and all four processed tables downloaded without login. The whole-exome deposit page loads but its file list was not retrievable, so that part is recorded as unavailable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: A fold-change column exists, but the lung tables contain only genes already called significant, so the negative class (genes that did not change) is absent and would have to be rebuilt by reprocessing raw sequencing reads from the archive.

a3_inputs_present.note: Rows carry Ensembl mouse gene identifiers plus chromosome, start, end, strand and length, so gene sequence features could be fetched; but no sequences are in the files themselves.

a4_units_stated.note: Columns are explicitly named FPKM (fragments per kilobase per million reads), raw counts, normalized counts, log2 fold change, p-value and adjusted p-value.

a5_enough_rows.note: Verified in the GEO records: 14 lung samples plus 8 macrophage samples = 22 biological units total, from one lab and one mouse strain. Treating genes as rows does not rescue it: the lung comparison supplies 772 significant genes with no non-significant genes, and the macrophage comparison 130.

a6_fits_laptop.note: All four tables together are tiny; the largest is a 54,532-gene expression matrix that loads in seconds.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No specific gene or sample counts in the text to contradict; the two series records and the files agree with each other. One internal oddity: the lung table has 10 raw-count columns but only 8 normalized ones.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are measured RNA abundances and a differential-expression statistic computed from them by the sequencing vendor, not another model's prediction.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be honestly trained here: the only claim available would be about which genes change in the lungs of four Men1-knockout mice from one laboratory, and the genes that did not change were never deposited.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene features to predict which genes change in expression when the tumour suppressor gene Men1 is deleted in mice.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would train on mouse genes described by their sequence and genomic position, labelled by whether their expression shifted after Men1 deletion. Verified counts: 772 significant genes in lung, 130 in macrophages, from 22 sequencing samples total.
plain_idea.predict: Direction and size of expression change (log2 fold change) on Men1 loss, measured by RNA sequencing of knockout versus wild-type mouse tissue in a single laboratory.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cancer-epigenetics labs studying menin and SETD2 would like to know which genes a scaffold protein controls, but with four knockout mice and no list of unchanged genes the question cannot be answered by a model here.

ml_idea: Predict Men1-knockout differential expression per gene from sequence and promoter features, validated across tissues. Dead on arrival: the deposited lung tables are filtered to significant genes only, so no negative class exists, and the whole experiment is 22 mouse samples from one lab.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the actual uncompressed file sizes I parsed (largest table 54,532 rows x 18 columns); no modelling was attempted because Part A failed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in GSE302950_Men1vsWT.xls.gz and check the adjusted p-value range: 772 rows, all Up or Down, which shows the unchanged genes were never deposited. Two minutes.

verdict_reason: A mechanism paper backed by 22 mouse RNA-sequencing samples; the deposited differential-expression tables contain only significant genes, so there is neither enough data (A5) nor a usable label column with negatives (A2).
